matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When moving a matchstick, keep its original orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal). Changing orientation would produce an invalid shape.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Apply this check whenever you relocate a stick, before finalizing the new symbols.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick and treating it as a horizontal stick, resulting in an invalid character.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick may be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During the transformation, ensure the total number of sticks stays constant.
matchstick.example: Removing a stick from a plus sign and not placing it elsewhere, effectively discarding a stick.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, every symbol must still be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a valid operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Check each character after the move to ensure it remains a valid symbol.
matchstick.example: After moving a stick, a V ends up missing one diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Convert the Roman numerals on both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers and ensure the equality holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have a candidate corrected equation, compute its numeric values to confirm it is a true equality.
matchstick.example: Proposing a corrected equation that still does not satisfy the arithmetic equality.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V each consist of exactly two diagonal sticks; after moving a stick, each must still contain both diagonals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a move involves X or V, ensure you do not remove or alter one of their diagonal sticks.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal stick out of an X, leaving it with only one diagonal, which is not a valid X.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must end with a line exactly matching 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>'. No extra whitespace or missing line is allowed.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After solving, format the answer with the required final line.
matchstick.example: Omitting the required final line or adding extra spaces, causing the answer to be rejected.

matchstick.title: Do not break I
matchstick.principle: When moving the only stick from an I (a single vertical stick), the I character must be removed entirely; you cannot leave a half I.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If you consider moving a stick from an I, ensure you either remove the whole I or keep it intact.
matchstick.example: Moving the only vertical stick from an I without removing the I, leaving an invalid fragment.

matchstick.title: Operator stick transformation
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from or to an operator (+, -, =), ensure the resulting operator is a valid symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any move that involves an operator must result in a recognized operator after the move.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from a plus sign and leaving the plus sign with only a horizontal stick, which is not a valid operator.

matchstick.title: Swap operators via horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: If the equation contains both '=' and '-' (or '+'), moving a single horizontal stick from '=' to '-' (or vice versa) can swap the operators while keeping them valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When both '=' and '-' (or '+') appear, consider moving a horizontal stick between them to swap their types.
matchstick.example: Attempting to swap '=' and '-' by moving a stick but ending up with an invalid operator such as a lone vertical line.

matchstick.title: Transfer vertical stick between I's
matchstick.principle: Moving a vertical stick from an I (which may disappear) to another numeral can increase that numeral's value, provided both source and target remain valid Roman numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to adjust values by adding or removing an I, consider moving a vertical stick from one I to another numeral.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from an I in a group of I's but leaving the source numeral with an invalid number of I's (e.g., creating 'IIII').

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model proposes a corrected equation without checking that the numeric values actually satisfy the equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always convert both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers after the move and confirm the equality before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model forgets to include the required final line or adds extra whitespace, causing the parser to miss the answer.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure the response ends with a line exactly matching 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>' with no extra spaces.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick away from a symbol but does not place it onto another symbol, effectively removing a stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When moving a stick, immediately decide its new location and update the target symbol accordingly.

matchstick.description: Breaking a numeral by moving a stick away, leaving an invalid shape (e.g., V with one diagonal, X with one diagonal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a numeral that requires that stick for its shape, resulting in an incomplete or invalid numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check the composition of each numeral before moving a stick; ensure the source numeral remains a valid Roman numeral after removal.

matchstick.description: Creating invalid Roman numeral (e.g., IIII, invalid ordering)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model adds or removes sticks in a way that produces a numeral with too many repeats or incorrect subtractive notation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any change, verify that each numeral follows standard Roman numeral rules (no more than three repeats, correct ordering, proper subtractive forms).
